claims.statement: Tom Allen came to St. Louis in about 1869 as a stranger, an Englishman sent to Billy Carroll as a man willing to fight anyone at any time.
claims.excerpt: Stranger, an Englishman who hed been sent here to Bilty Carroll as-one willing to Geht any

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Mike McCoole on Foster's Island on June 15, 1869 for $1,000 a side; after nine rounds Jack Smith hit Allen in the eye with a stake and McCoole's backers cut the ropes and broke into the ring.
claims.excerpt: Jsaek Smith, who stood near the ropes, pulled upa stuke and hit Allen in the eye with it

claims.statement: Referee Val McKinney decided the Allen and McCoole fight in McCoole's favour.
claims.excerpt: He decided thin in favor of McCovle

claims.statement: Tom Allen and Charley Gallagher fought fifty miles from St. Louis on August 17, 1869 for $1,000 a side, and the referee declared the fight a draw.
claims.excerpt: tought fifty miles from St. Louis, Avgust 17, 1869, was another barney

claims.statement: Charley Gallagher struck Tom Allen as Allen came forward to shake hands, and Allen jumped the ropes and fled the ring.

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Mace, the English champion, near New Orleans in 1870 for $2,500 a side and lost; Mace was given the fight.
claims.excerpt: He played it good, and) Mace wus given the fight.

claims.statement: Tom Allen was seen drunk a few days before the Mace fight and entered the ring heavier than his usual 175 pounds (figure garbled).

claims.statement: Tom Allen got half the excursion money from the Mace fight and had to split it with his backers Billy Carroll and John Franklin.
claims.excerpt: which he had to divide with bis back;ners, Billy Carroll and John Franklin

fights.notes: The paper says referee Val McKinney was paid $700 by McCoole's backers (Jack Looney and Tom Kehoe) to decide for McCoole; the payment is not Allen's act and is not recorded as a claim.

fights.notes: Disagrees with the 1882 article printed on 2 January (643), which says Allen won in eleven rounds. Referee Larry Wessel.

fights.excerpt: He played it good, and) Mace wus given the fight.
fights.notes: Allen claimed his arm was broken after being thrown; the paper says Carroll knew it was not broken. Mace's first name is not given.

notes: The McCoole referee bribery and the Coburn-Mace matches are not about Allen and are left out.
